findings.text: follow-on: the fragment states "Verdict tally: 5 reuse, 3 adapt, 1 absent-and-build capability classes across the rows" and the run manifest's artifacts line repeats it as "verdicts 5 reuse / 3 adapt / 1 absent-and-build at row level", but neither number is reproducible from the map's own row-verdict column, which is 3 reuse (rows 2, 6, 8), 4 adapt (rows 1, 3, 4, 9) and 2 absent-and-build (rows 5, 7). The fragment hedges ("rows carry mixed verdicts; the row-level summary table is the authority") but still prints a tally a reader cannot reproduce, and the manifest's "at row level" is outright false; a coordinator routing dispatch from the headline is told five capability classes can be reused when three can, and that one must be built when two must. Not blocking because the authoritative row table is correct and a reader who follows it gets the right split.

follow-on: two citations name a symbol that is not on the line cited: nova/nova/imas/equilibrium.py:688 is cited for `plot_tri`, whose def is at :686 (line 688 is the set_axes call inside it), and imas-efit/src/EFIT/null_detection.f90:36 is cited for `find_all_nulls`, whose subroutine is at :406 (line 36 is the tail of the module docstring, which the map does describe as "module header lines 1-36"). Both pass the bounds-only gate and both symbols do exist in the cited files, so no reference is fabricated; the imprecision is only that the cited line is not the symbol's line.

follow-on: the citation gate matches only backticked `repo/path:line` and silently skips the map's shorthand ``:NNNN`` form (11 instances, e.g. the ``:1132``/``:3389`` on row 4 and the helper lines in the row-4 detail), so 74 is a floor on the citation surface and a wrong-but-in-range shorthand line would pass. A path-aware form that resolves shorthand against the preceding full path (as both my checks do) would close it. The gate should also be committed beside the map so a later reader can re-run it, since the map's whole value is that its citations resolve.

The reviewed artifact is documentation only, so the citation gate and its mutation control are the node's whole gate surface. I reproduced the head arm (74/0 EXIT=0), the baseline arm (66/9 EXIT=1, same ids) and a mutation of my own (73/1 EXIT=1, refused) in fresh processes.

justifications.durability: the map is a read-only markdown artifact and nothing in the tree guards it. The citation gate that is its only check lives in the run directory (/home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261001T215616124162-ctta-prior-art-scout/verify_citations.py), not in the repository, so no test, fixture or CI step re-runs it; the map will rot silently as the very lines it cites move, and the files it cites (nova/equilibrium/flux_surface_connectivity.py, connectivity_boundary.py, stencil_nulls.py) are exactly the ones §2–§4 are about to rewrite. The core two claims — the row-verdict tally and the citation set — have no re-derivation in-tree. Not lower because a docs-only survey legitimately has limited durable surface and the gate itself is recorded and reproducible.

I then went beyond the node's own gate, which checks only that the cited line number is in range: a symbol-content pass over the 51 citations that name a symbol found 48 with the named token on the cited line, and an 11-citation pass over the shorthand ``:NNNN`` form the gate does not match found all 11 resolving with their symbol present. I verified the cross-repo headline claims directly against imas-efit: contour_tree.f90 is 4131 lines, build_contour_tree at :130, build_contour_tree_with_wall at :1132, mark_private_subtrees at :1673 and merge_tree_decide at :3389 all match (grep of the subroutine lines), and output/m2-build/mergetree_oracle/merge_tree.py exists with the born-earlier tie-break comment at :189. Deduction: the gate is bounds-only and skips the shorthand form, so it cannot catch a wrong-but-in-range citation, and two such exist (see findings).
